known_issues.title: Beamos scorch marks last a few ticks longer
known_issues.detail: Hot_Floor 231 under a Beamos beam fades a few ticks later at 60: its own heat and fade are stepped as at 30 (the beam sets it each step, cLib_chaseF up 5 a tick while hit, down 0.4 after); the beam's half-step positions sweep a scorch once more than 30's whole-tick jumps do and add heat (finer sampling of the beam's path, like the water jar's edge): left as inherent (session bottom)

known_issues.title: A thrown water jar can break on an edge 30 misses
known_issues.detail: Dragon Roost room 8: thrown from about 100 units further back, the jar breaks on the floor's edge at 60 but in the lava at 30; 60's finer sampling catches an edge 30's step jumps over Decided (session bottom): inherent to the finer sampling (the jar moves on 30's ticks; its arc grazes the edge between two of them, where a 60 step lands), left.

known_issues.title: Ganon's Tower trial: the magma rocks' bob differs
known_issues.detail: The walk-in ends on 30's tick, and the rocks bob correctly on their own lava. The lava's bubbles come from the random stream, which parts from 30's before the warp: Outset's fishman picks his swim animation in a one-frame window that 30's ticks step over and 60's half steps land in, and his path is 0.7-1.6 units off from the start. After that every draw differs, so the bubbles do too. Not syncable: recorded (session bottom).

known_issues.title: Link: an action can change a tick off after his path drifts
known_issues.detail: Fixed: the turn in place and waiting start on 30's ticks; the turn while moving (a tick early), the swim's surfacing (a tick late) and a slash's next action (the spin's charge after a left slash, half a tick early) come on 30's ticks. Left: an action that starts at a threshold (a ledge reached, a turn's last 8000-unit step, a wall) can come a tick apart once his path is a few units or a degree off 30's, as in routes sidle and tour's corner

known_issues.title: Random-driven enemies drift from the 30 fps run
known_issues.detail: Random-driven enemies (Magtail waits, Peahat flights) drift from the 30 fps run, as expected

known_issues.title: Pots, sidling and ladders: fixed
known_issues.detail: Checked tick by tick at 30 and 60. Fixed: a thrown pot sank too fast in water (now within 0.2 units), sidling ran up to 2.3 units ahead (now on 30's ticks), sidling round a corner was stuck at 60 (now turns on 30's tick), a turn while carrying ended half a tick early (now on 30's tick), and lifting's hand-over to carrying came a tick late (fixed by Link's exact animation frame). Lifting, carrying, turning, walking and throwing a pot, and a ladder up and down, now match 30

known_issues.title: Windfall at night: the auction fixed
known_issues.detail: The lights converted (night via WWHD_DEBUG_TIME=905:345). The auction's bidders and the auction (361, 382) are 30's at every tick by night but for IDs given at their creation (session bottom); the bidding ran twice as fast at 60 and is now once a tick: the six bids and the choice on 30's ticks, the bid's call a tick early left (session top). Type 259, thought to be shutters, is Windfall's HD-only bunting line: its cloth never moves and it matches 30 every tick (session bottom)

known_issues.title: Enemies falling into water
known_issues.detail: Fixed for open water: at 60 the half step after an enemy reached the water went on sinking, so a Moblin ran 13.5 units deeper than 30's; now the tick ends at the surface as at 30, and Moblins and Bokoblins sink on 30's heights. The hang at the Outset dock's edge is the dock itself (30's Moblin is pushed out of its side for a tick), not the water check

queue_note: Round 14 (week 2, from 2026-10-09): performance for the Steam Deck and Android (B75), then the rival's lessons. Goal: full speed at 60 on the worker (power-capped, the Deck's stand-in); it reaches ~54 fps there with 3 CPU threads, GPU-bound. Two lanes, each worked from its top down: top (CPU side and turning the speed flags on by default) and bottom (GPU side, upscalers (FSR 1, then FSR 3.1/4, XeSS, DLSS: the owner's ask) and graphics options); main routes, deploys and keeps the docs; qa takes only problems the others are stuck on. Complexity 1-10 in brackets. On the owner's PC: ww-4 9385d6d.

queue.name: Round 14: [8] Three host threads by default (WWHD_CORES=3; 47 -> 54 fps on the worker): routes 3 against 1 on every predeploy route, a 1 h real-time soak, the locks list, per-core figures in the log; then on by default with full gates

Round 14: [4] Skip the title in test runs (the owner's ask): WWHD_DEBUG_BOOT=slot loads a save straight into play (no title, no file select), for the real-time routes, soaks and A/Bs (under load the title's fixed-frame press is missed and most runs replay); fallback: the press held until the file select shows; the deterministic checks keep the title (their reference has it)

Round 14: [3] Frame rate cap 30/40/50/60 in the settings (the owner's ask): 30 and 60 exact as today; 40 and 50 at 60 ticks' logic with a fixed pattern of dropped half-tick frames (keep-speed's machinery: full speed, slightly uneven motion, said in the option); smooth 40/50 comes with uncapped (D21 step 4); keep full speed always on in real time, no option (the owner, 2026-10-09)

Round 14: [5] Full speed below 30 (the owner's ask): when even whole-tick frames run late, skip their rendering too (the logic and actor draws still run, as keep-speed's dropped half frames), so a slow machine shows fewer frames at full speed; never skip a frame something reads back (the picto box, queries); a floor on frames shown; helps when rendering is the bottleneck (logic slower than 30 ticks a second can't keep speed)

Round 14: [7] The lazy GX2DrawDone by default (deck-plan item 2; -15% game thread): A/B on the desktop worker with a window, vsync on and off; a sync-validation run with it; then on by default with full gates

Round 14: [5] Frame skipping's shown frames cost ~85 ms against ~48 ms in plain 30 (render-bound worker: 11.6 fps shown where ~20 should fit): find what piles into the shown frame (the GPU catching up, texture uploads) and fix it, so slow machines show as many frames as fit
Round 14: [6] Texture write-watch in real time (WWHD_WRITE_WATCH=1, deck-plan item 6): worker A/B of its gain, a soak with verify mode (0 misses), then on by default
Round 14: [9] A guest buffer cache (rival-study 9.3 #3): skip the per-frame vertex copy (~16% of the render thread) for buffers write-watch saw unchanged
Round 14: [5] The half step's journal: the inline check in RT_STORE (deck-plan item 5's rest, ~1% of the game thread)
Round 14: [6] 30 fps on the worker reaches only 27-28.7 fps: find where the time goes and fix it
Round 14: [9] The recompiled code itself (82% of the game thread, flat): registers kept in host registers, a real-time build without the cycle counting, -O3; measure each on the worker

Round 14: [5] Measure the GPU on the worker (gpu-plan item 1): WWHD_GPU_TIMING and gpu-clock.sh on its iGPU under the power cap; reconcile the ~18.7 ms a frame with the desktop's 1.38 ms; the per-pass table into gpu-plan.md

Round 14: [6] Narrow barriers and surface fit by default (gpu-plan item 2): the worker A/Bs the cloud sessions left, then on by default with full gates (narrow also removes the default's 71 sync hazards)
Round 14: [7] Render scale: worker A/B on en-tn at 100/75/50%, then dynamic resolution that holds 60 (gpu-plan item 3)

Round 14: [5] FSR 1 upscaling (EASU + RCAS sharpening, MIT, any GPU) on top of render scale and dynamic resolution, between the 3D scene and the HUD so text stays native; a settings option; A/B quality at 75/50% on the worker

Round 14: [9] The temporal upscalers' inputs, from the recomp: per-model motion vectors (each draw's previous and current transforms), a sub-pixel camera jitter in the projection, depth, a reactive mask for effects; the game's own bloom, depth of field and AO kept right; 30 and the checks unchanged when off
Round 14: [7] FSR 3.1 upscaling (open, Vulkan, any GPU) on b-motion's inputs; a settings option (quality, balanced, performance); its frame generation is b-framegen

Round 14: [8] Frame generation as an opt-in (the owner's ask; off by default, labelled as generated frames over the true 60): FSR 3.1's frame generation (any GPU) on b-motion's inputs with the HUD kept out of the interpolation, e.g. 60 real -> 120 shown; its added latency stated in the option; DLSS frame generation (RTX 40+) after
Round 14: [6] The GPU's other exact wins (gpu-plan item 2's rest): load ops instead of clears, redundant transitions
Round 14: [8] Shaders optimised offline (gpu-plan item 5) from the D20 shader list
Round 14: [7] Widescreen (Hor+) and HUD anchoring (rival-study 9.3 #7)
Round 14: [5] Graphics options: the ambient occlusion toggle (find the pass), anisotropic filtering, FXAA (gpu-plan item 4's rest, rival-study #8)
Round 14: [2] Week 2's setup: GitHub's only branch is main, the worktrees on main with their worker settings, the two-lane queue on this page
Round 14: [2] The docs current: deck-plan's item table, gpu-plan's landed items, the handoff's head (three threads, render scale, presets)
Round 14: [4] A batched deploy of main to the owner's PC (predeploy 0 FAIL plus gohmatail gohmarock), then after each lane's landings
Round 14: [3] With the owner: the Deck's quick tests (deck-plan tests 1-4: clocks, 30 fps, a profile, thread placement) on the newest deploy

later: FSR 4 (parked 2026-10-10 after bottom's evaluation): AMD ships it only as a signed DirectX 12 DLL (SDK 2.3); the community Vulkan ports use a leaked model we can't ship. Waiting for AMD's Vulkan FSR 4; FSR 3.1's inputs (HUD split, motion, jitter) fit it; revisit at each SDK release
XeSS (parked 2026-10-10): Intel ships it only as closed Windows DLLs (no Linux library); for the Windows platform work, on FSR 3.1's inputs

DLSS (parked 2026-10-10, the owner's call): NVIDIA's RTX SDK licence forbids its files in our public repo (distribution only as object code; not under an open-source licence); a compliant route exists (nothing NVIDIA in git, an optional local SDK path at build time, our glue code under MPL); needs an NVIDIA GPU to test
Platforms: Linux arm64, Windows, Android and CI through cloud sessions on github.com/flossbud/WWHDRecomp (docs/cloud-handoff.md)
Android-specific speed: ADPF hints, core pinning, thermal (deck-plan), once the port runs
More of the rival's lessons (rival-study 9.3): save states, a constant guest memory base, draw batching, interpolation as a low-power mode
Uncapped frame rate (D21 step 4), built on the half steps: when the owner says
The owner's extensive testing and repair
